clue.text: Show forbearance

definitions.meaning: a stage show: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera of that name, about aesthetes and dragoons
forbearance is calm endurance of delay or provocation

explanation.surface: An instruction to be tolerant and hold back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a verb telling you to display forbearance, but it is a noun: the title of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: one sense is an operetta title, the other is the quality of tolerant waiting.

clue.text: He can carry drink

definitions.meaning: a person employed to carry luggage, as at a station or hotel
a dark brown beer brewed from charred malt

explanation.surface: A man who can hold his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone who can carry his drink well; split it into a luggage carrier and a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a luggage carrier at a hotel, and a dark stout-like beer, share the one name.

clue.text: Competent to enter race for inscribed panel

indicators.note: to enter means the word for competent goes inside the race's letters

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
competent means able

explanation.surface: A capable entrant joins a race for a commemorative plaque.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone or metal slab bearing an inscription is called by this name, as with the tablets of the law.

clue.text: Measure old apparel without omission

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure, half an em
tire is an archaic word for attire or clothing

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up old clothes thoroughly, leaving nothing out.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is the printer's unit of width; TIRE survives as the old short form of attire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with nothing omitted is whole and complete, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Map to employ again after drink

parts.note: a map, especially a nautical one, is a chart
to employ again is to reuse

explanation.surface: Someone plans to reuse a map after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A green or yellow herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks, so an example of a drink.

clue.text: Glib talk more exactly to the purpose

definitions.meaning: smooth, rapid salesman's or comedian's chatter
the comparative of pat, meaning apt or exactly fitting

explanation.surface: Smooth chat that is more pertinent than it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the letters as pat plus -er: something more pat is more neatly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a noun for fluent chatter and a comparative adjective meaning more apposite.

clue.text: Evaluate Paris fashion without copy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for copy wraps round the rest

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate

indicators.note: fashion as a verb, to shape or remake, signals the letters of Paris are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic judges Paris fashion as wholly original, with no copying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here it has its old sense of outside, so the word for copy wraps round the reworked city name.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess the value or quality of something, a direct synonym of evaluate.

clue.text: Actor writing article on Spain, perhaps

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: perhaps suggests Spain is only one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A performer writes a piece about Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts THE above SPIAN, the letters of SPAIN reworked; 'writing' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is a stage performer, named after Thespis, the legendary first Greek actor.

clue.text: Feeling less anxious when deputy has taken over

definitions.meaning: a sentry or worker is ... when a replacement takes over the duty

explanation.surface: Someone is relieved of stress once a stand-in arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: eased of anxiety, and replaced at one's post by a substitute.

clue.text: Refutation of argument about singer and a novice

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Dame Clara Butt, the celebrated English contralto
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A rebuttal about a singer and a beginner in some dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Clara Butt was a famous English contralto of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a counter-argument that sets out to disprove a claim, so a refutation.

clue.text: Point in dismay to supplication

indicators.note: in places the compass point inside the word for dismay

parts.note: to appal is to dismay or horrify
E, east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone, aghast, turns to begging.
explanation.definitionFit: An appeal is an earnest request or plea, which is what a supplication is.

clue.text: Curse old city and shed tear

parts.note: ex means former
EC, the postal district of the City of London

indicators.note: shed as in broken up or cast apart, signalling the letters of tear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone damns an ancient city and weeps.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the City of London's postcode area; 'shed' tells you to rework TEAR into RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down curses upon, a formal synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Specimen of Southern Liberal

parts.note: liberal in the sense of generous or plentiful, ample

explanation.surface: A typical example of a southern Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the political party, but it means generous, plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a small representative part taken for study, the same as a specimen.

clue.text: It makes for resilience to set up market on River Nile, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the word for market is read upwards

parts.note: a mart is a market
the Po, the river of northern Italy

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of Nile could be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan to set up a market beside the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAM is MART read upwards; the Nile is a red herring, as 'River' gives PO and 'perhaps' reworks NILE into LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a springy canvas sheet for bouncing, so a device that produces resilience.

clue.text: Flower centres have freedom from disturbance

parts.note: hearts are the centres or cores of things
ease is freedom from trouble or disturbance

explanation.surface: The core of a flower brings peace of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartsease is the wild pansy, a small flower; the name also means peace of mind.

clue.text: Man watching vehicle for leaders

parts.note: a van is a goods vehicle
a guard is a man keeping watch

explanation.surface: A security man keeps an eye on a van for his bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: The vanguard is the foremost part of an army or movement, those who lead the way.

clue.text: Worker in clear at banana plant

indicators.note: in tells you the worker goes inside the word for clear

parts.note: plain means clear or obvious
an ant, the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer stands in a clearing by a banana plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a tropical plant bearing a starchy banana-like fruit used in cooking.

clue.text: Heartbroken figure may be menace

indicators.note: broken means the letters of heart are smashed and rearranged

parts.note: ten is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A heartbroken person may become a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartbroken' reads as one word of the surface, but it splits into fodder and an anagram signal ('broken').
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten is to menace, both verbs meaning to intimidate with a hint of harm.

clue.text: Still no variations?

definitions.meaning: still in the sense of nevertheless or even so
literally everything identical, with nothing differing

explanation.surface: A question whether nothing has changed at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: an idiom meaning nevertheless, and a literal phrase meaning everything identical.

clue.text: Argument on what society girl took in

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, a young woman entering high society
ate, took in food

explanation.surface: A dispute over what a debutante had for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal discussion of opposing views, so an argument in the sense of a dispute.

clue.text: He vacillates with noose

definitions.meaning: one who halts or wavers, hesitating
a rope with a running loop, as used for hanging or leading a horse

explanation.surface: A man hesitates before the hangman's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: one who hesitates, and a rope or strap, especially a hangman's rope.

clue.text: Stiffness of celebrity at church

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous person grows stiff at a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch figuratively means stiffness or formality of manner, from the stiffening agent for cloth.

clue.text: Turning embarrassed after information on sex discrimination

indicators.note: after places the reversed word for embarrassed behind the information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: turning means the word for embarrassed is read backwards

parts.note: red, as in red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: Someone flushes after hearing facts about sex discrimination.
explanation.walkthrough: The British slang word for information comes first; 'Turning' reads the colour of embarrassment backwards, and 'after' sets that behind it. 'discrimination' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender is often used as a synonym for a person's sex, male or female.

clue.text: Is unable to include cooker in agreement

indicators.note: to include means the word for is unable contains the cooker

parts.note: can't, is unable, without the apostrophe
an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: Someone cannot fit a cooker into a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding agreement, as in a deed or treaty.

clue.text: Makes adjustments for girl having second thoughts about head teacher

parts.note: Ada, a girl's name

indicators.note: about means the postscript letters go round the teacher's first letter

parts.note: PS, a postscript, added as an afterthought

indicators.note: head takes only the first letter of teacher

explanation.surface: A girl rethinks her view of the headmistress and changes her ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to modify or adjust something to suit new conditions.

clue.text: Underworld flower of calamity

parts.note: Dis, the Roman god of the underworld and his realm
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A flower from the underworld spells doom.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden great misfortune, the same as a calamity.

clue.text: Clamour a book brought to Belgian town

parts.note: din is a loud clamour
NT, the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A noisy book launch in a Belgian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinant is a town on the Meuse in southern Belgium, so an example of a Belgian town.

clue.text: Seer turning coy on investigation

indicators.note: turning here means the letters of seer are shuffled around

parts.note: arch means playfully sly or coy

explanation.surface: A prophet turns shy when looked into.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic investigation to establish facts, a direct synonym.
